expected.name: Alfred Marder
expected.description: Alfred Marder was a New Haven printer, union activist, and one of the Connecticut Communists prosecuted in the New Haven Smith Act case. After an earlier indictment was dismissed because the grand jury had been improperly selected, he was re-indicted in March 1955. A jury acquitted him on March 29, 1956. Arrested May 29, 1954 in the Connecticut Smith Act roundup. On June 16, 1954, he remained in New Haven County Jail because he could not raise bail; the previous day his bail had been reduced from $20,000 to $10,000. He was subsequently released on bail, and a February 23, 1955 court ruling confirms that all seven original defendants were then at liberty. His exact jail admission and release dates, and total time detained, remain unverified.

Lucy Gellman / New Haven Arts, Alfred Marder at the 2020 William Lanson statue unveiling. Cropped to isolate Marder.

Documented pretrial detention

Arrested May 29, 1954 in the Connecticut Smith Act roundup. On June 16, 1954, he remained in New Haven County Jail because he could not raise bail; the previous day his bail had been reduced from $20,000 to $10,000. He was subsequently released on bail, and a February 23, 1955 court ruling confirms that all seven original defendants were then at liberty. His exact jail admission and release dates, and total time detained, remain unverified.

Sources: Manchester Evening Herald, June 16, 1954, page 14, “State Reds Unable To Raise Cut Bail”; United States v. Silverman, February 23, 1955, 129 F. Supp. 496, 514; UConn Archives, original seven-defendant leaflet (May 29 arrest date and identities).
